$comment: First slice of the HITL escalation design (issue #1187, decision-tier rule
at #1187 comment 5800142871, Fable second opinion at #1187 comment
5800683025). `scripts/land-stack.mjs` reads this file to classify a pull
request's changed-file set into a tier, and to refuse to merge a tier-1 or
tier-2 pull request whose review evidence does not satisfy the rule below.
This is a merge-train gate, not a CI workflow: it costs no GitHub Actions
minutes, calls no model, and waits on nothing, matching AGENTS.md's
'Model-assisted code review is manually initiated' rule word for word --
see docs/HITL.md for why the record requirement lives here instead of in
verify-standards.yml.
TIER CLASSIFICATION IS A UNION-OVER-PATHS, MAX-OVER-TIERS OPERATION, OVER
ONE PULL REQUEST'S OWN DIFF. Every changed path in a pull request is
classified independently against tier2.globs, then tier1.globs minus
tier1RecordExempt.globs; the pull request's overall tier is the HIGHEST
tier any single path reaches. Spreading a change across many files never
lowers its tier below what one file alone would demand. KNOWN GAP
(#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 15): for a merge-train BATCH pull
request stacking several already-approved constituent PRs, only the
batch PR's own diff (against its own base) is classified today --
classifying the union of every constituent PR's own diff individually is
not implemented in this slice. In practice a batch PR's diff already
contains every constituent's changes relative to the batch's base, so
this still catches a tier-1/tier-2 path somewhere in the stack; what it
does NOT do is attribute a finding to which constituent PR introduced it,
or classify a constituent against ITS OWN base rather than the batch's.
Scaled back here rather than left overclaimed.
THIS FILE, AND THE REST OF THE ENFORCEMENT SURFACE IT DEFINES, ARE
TIER-2, NOT TIER-1 (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 13). A tier-1
change (two independent reviewers, neither the owner) could otherwise
narrow tier2.globs -- for example removing governance/model-
qualifications/** from it -- and downgrade the owner-only boundary
without the owner ever being involved. tier2.globs below therefore
names this file itself, scripts/land-stack.mjs and its test (the code
that reads and enforces it), docs/contracts/decision-record.json and
scripts/check-decision-records.mjs and its test (the decision-record
contract and validator the tier-2 gate also runs inline -- see
'RUN CHECK-DECISION-RECORDS INSIDE THE GATE' below), package-scope.json
(the publishing scope -- CLAUDE.md's own rule already treats it as the
one place that value lives), and scripts/lib/** (helper modules a
check:*.mjs or land-stack.mjs itself imports, previously a known,
acknowledged gap -- Fable's point 2 and #1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
should-fix 13 -- now closed by moving the whole directory to tier-2
rather than trying to name only the gate-relevant subset by hand).
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM governance/merge-policy.json: that file's
own $comment declares it 'THE ONE PLACE THIS REPOSITORY'S PERMITTED MERGE
METHODS ARE DECLARED' -- a narrowly scoped drift-alarm for GitHub's own
merge-method setting. Review-tier classification is a different policy
domain (what evidence a change needs, not which merge button is used), so
it gets its own file rather than widening merge-policy.json's declared
scope. scripts/land-stack.mjs reads both.
GOVERNANCE/DECISIONS/** IS TIER-1, NOT TIER-0 (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
blocking finding 4). An earlier version of this file exempted decision
records from every tier as 'a pure record file with its own rules' --
that made 'run check-decision-records inside the gate' (below) the ONLY
thing standing between an unreviewed pull request and a self-issued
'owner' decision record that then authorizes a real tier-2 change,
reviewed by nobody. Decision records are no longer exempt: adding or
changing one requires the same tier-1 independent-review bar as any
other governance path, on top of (not instead of) the shape validation
below.
RUN CHECK-DECISION-RECORDS INSIDE THE GATE (#1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
blocking findings 4 and 5). scripts/land-stack.mjs imports
`validateDecisionRecordShape` and `isRelaxationPastSunset` directly from
scripts/check-decision-records.mjs (not a re-implementation) and applies
them at two points: `evaluateChangedDecisionRecords` refuses ANY pull
request (any tier) that adds or edits a malformed governance/decisions/
*.json file, and `evaluateTier2Decision` refuses to treat a record as
tier-2 authority at all unless it is itself schema-valid, `tier: "tier-2"`
(a tier-1 record is never tier-2 authority), not superseded by a later
record, and not a relaxation past its own sunset -- and treats an
unparseable `expiry` as already expired, never as unexpired.
KNOWN GAPS REMAINING (see docs/HITL.md 'Honour-system limits' for the
full discussion): this classifies files named in the pull request's own
declared diff, paginated directly against the REST Pulls API (never
`gh pr view --json files`, which silently truncates past 100 entries --
#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, blocking finding 3) and cross-checked against
the pull request's own `changedFiles` count, refusing to classify at all
on a mismatch or an empty list. It still does not reach a `package.json`
`scripts` VALUE beyond the file itself being tier-1 -- a tier-1 reviewer
still has to actually read the diff of that file, the same as any other
tier-1 path; this file draws the path boundary, not the review quality.
BOOTSTRAP (#1187 review at df15ab87, should-fix 9; CORRECTED #1187
review round 6, second reviewer, blocking): this file, once this pull
request adds it, does not exist on `main` until this very pull request
merges. Every pull request `scripts/land-stack.mjs` classifies before
that merge -- including the one that adds this file -- reads a base ref
where `governance/review-tiers.json` 404s, and
`defaultReadReviewTierConfig` still throws internally when that read
fails. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS COMMENT STOPPED THERE, describing
that throw as fail-closed and claiming this pull request could never
pass `land-stack.mjs --status` against itself and that its first
landing was necessarily a plain `gh pr merge`. Round 6 added report-only
fail-open handling in `runStatus` (see docs/HITL.md's "Enforcement:
report-only, then enforce"): the throw from an unreadable base config
is now caught by the same try/catch that wraps the whole tier
evaluation, `enforcement` cannot be determined from a config that never
loaded and so defaults to "report-only", and the resulting failure is
reported as a warning rather than thrown or refused. THIS PULL REQUEST
CAN NOW PASS `land-stack.mjs --status` AGAINST ITSELF, under
report-only, precisely because report-only is built to tolerate the
absence of a prior config to classify against. A plain, owner-approved
`gh pr merge` (the documented skip path, docs/HITL.md) remains
available and is how an owner would land this file under enforce, but
it is no longer the ONLY path now that report-only is the default.
This same fallback is also an ENFORCE-MODE gap this repository has not
yet resolved: if `main`'s own config here says "enforce" but the read
of it fails for any reason, the landing still proceeds as report-only
regardless -- see docs/HITL.md's "Before switching to enforce"
checklist. Every later change to this file goes through the gate
normally, once a prior version of it exists on `main` to read.
$enforcementComment: SHIP REPORT-ONLY FIRST (coordinator decision, round 5, matching this
repository's report-then-enforce pattern -- see e.g. verify-standards.yml's
own rollout history). `scripts/land-stack.mjs` reads THIS field from the
pull request's BASE ref (never the head -- a pull request cannot flip its
own enforcement switch by editing this file on its own branch) and always
computes and prints the full tier verdict and every refusal reason, but
only actually BLOCKS a merge when this value is the literal string
"enforce". Any other value, including a missing field, an unrecognized
string, or a read failure, is treated as "report-only": fail-OPEN on the
switch itself (never fail-closed into silently blocking merges nobody
asked this gate to block yet), but fail-CLOSED on everything the gate
actually reasons about once enforcement is on -- the switch changes
nothing about the underlying tier/independence/decision-record logic.
ROLLOUT PLAN (see docs/HITL.md for the fuller discussion): the owner
observes a week of real report-only verdicts printed against real merges
-- did the tier split look right, did any true tier-2 change almost land
without a decision record, did anything get misclassified -- before
flipping this to "enforce". CHANGING THIS VALUE IS ITSELF A TIER-2
CHANGE: this file is already in tier2.globs below (the enforcement
surface, not merely its own contents), so flipping the switch on still
requires an owner decision record, the same as narrowing a tier-2 glob
would. This is deliberate: turning ON a gate that can block real merges
is exactly the kind of consequential, hard-to-reverse-in-practice change
the decision-tier rule means by tier 2, even though turning it OFF again
later would be comparatively cheap.
TESTS MUST EXERCISE ENFORCE MODE (coordinator instruction, round 5):
scripts/land-stack.test.mjs's `applyEnforcement` tests cover both modes
directly, and its `runStatus`-level tests exercise at least one refusal
under `enforcement: "enforce"` end to end, not only the pure function in
isolation -- a report-only-only test suite could not catch a wiring bug
that left the enforce path unreachable.

$comment: Gate and check scripts, CI workflow definitions, formal contracts,
governance policy (minus the record-shaped files carved out below),
and the handful of root documents that state this repository's public
safety and contribution rules. Matches the tier-1 path description in
BROADENED FROM A HAND-MAINTAINED SCRIPT LIST (#1187 review round 4,
blocking finding 1): an earlier version of this file named only
scripts/check-*.mjs plus a handful of other files by hand, which left
gate-critical code entirely UNCLASSIFIED (tier-0, no review needed at
all) -- .github/scripts/*.mjs (assemble-verify-inputs.mjs,
collect-credential-evidence.mjs, collect-secret-scan-observation.mjs),
the two .github/*policy*.json files verify-standards.yml reads,
.root-entry-policy.json, scripts/push-tree-identical.mjs, and the
publish path (now tier-2, see below). The Fable second opinion's point
2(b) predicted exactly this: 'check scripts is porous'.
'scripts/**' and '.github/**' now cover the WHOLE surface a workflow
can execute or read, deliberately over-inclusive rather than
hand-enumerated -- every ordinary dev script under scripts/ becomes
tier-1 too, which is friction, not a safety hole; only tier-2's
narrower, hand-picked publish-path list (below) needs to stay precise.
scripts/check-workflow-references.test.mjs's own test
'every script/config path referenced by a workflow classifies at
least tier-1' (scripts/land-stack.test.mjs) is the enforcement for
this claim: it scans every .github/workflows/*.yml file for a
referenced scripts/**/*.mjs or .github/**/*.{mjs,json} path and fails
if classifyTier ever returns tier-0 for one, so this file cannot drift
back into being porous without a failing test saying so. THE
ENFORCEMENT SURFACE ITSELF -- land-stack.mjs, this file, the
decision-record contract/validator, package-scope.json, and
scripts/lib/** -- is tier-2, not tier-1 (already inside 'scripts/**'
but elevated by the max-over-tiers rule); see this file's own header
comment for why.
Exactly the independence rule at #1187 comment 5800142871, tightened
by #1187 review at 8e6d97ea (blocking findings 1-2, should-fix 9):
- Exactly ONE current-head role:"author" record must exist. More than
one is ambiguous and refused outright -- never resolved to 'the
first one found', which would let a second author-role record
quietly count as an independent reviewer.
- ANY current-head independent reviewer record whose state is
'reject' or 'changes-requested' refuses the merge immediately and
is NEVER outvoted by a later approving pair from other reviewers --
'If they disagree, or either says reject, escalate to the owner
with both positions', and 'tier-1 reviewers disagree' is listed
under 'escalate immediately, whatever the tier'.
- Otherwise, a qualifying pair requires: state 'approved' on both
records ('commented' never counts -- the rule requires 'both
recommend acceptance'); one record 'primary' depth and the other
'secondary' depth (the rule's own 'a first reviewer plus a
stronger-model second opinion' pairing -- two 'primary' records do
not satisfy it); distinct instanceId from each other and from the
author; and differing model or provider.
Enforced by scripts/land-stack.mjs's evaluateTier1Independence against
structured `foundry-review-record` comments (docs/contracts/
review-record.json) at the pull request's EXACT current head -- a
record whose headSha does not match the live head is stale and not
treated as current evidence, the same staleness discipline #1311
established for GitHub's own native reviews. A record from a comment
EDITED after it was posted, or from a comment this repository could
not confirm as an admin/write collaborator's, REFUSES THE WHOLE GATE
outright rather than being silently dropped (docs/contracts/
review-record.json's own 'REFUSING THE GATE' and 'AUTHORIZATION'
sections; #1187 review round 4 tightened this past the original
#1187 review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 11 fix, which only dropped the
record rather than refusing the gate). A reject/changes-requested
record is additionally STICKY once authorized and current -- see
docs/contracts/review-record.json's own 'A REJECT IS STICKY' section.
'governance/ (minus pure record files, which have their own rules)'
(#1187 comment 5800142871). Every path below is committed evidence or
history -- appended to, or replaced wholesale by a script, never
hand-edited as policy -- and each already has its own gate (release
readiness, qualification-record-required, package-identity checks,
etc.) enforcing its shape. Requiring a second independent reviewer on
top of an existing automated gate for a pure record write would not
buy additional safety, only friction.
governance/decisions/** is DELIBERATELY NOT listed here (#1187 review
at 8e6d97ea, blocking finding 4) -- see this file's own header
comment. It is tier-1 like any other governance/** path, on top of
(not instead of) scripts/check-decision-records.mjs's own shape
validation, which land-stack.mjs runs inline regardless of tier.
governance/model-qualifications/ is intentionally NOT listed here --
it is promoted to tier-2 below instead of merely staying tier-1,
because every row in it requires per-model owner approval by design
(see docs/HITL.md and governance/model-qualifications/allowlist.json).
'define tier-2 globs for paths the owner reserves (rulesets or
settings-as-code, if any exist; propose them)' (task instruction).
Measured against this repository's own tree today (2026-09-23):
no branch-ruleset or repository-settings-as-code file exists IN this
git tree -- governance/merge-policy.json's own $comment says why:
'the merge methods a repository offers live in GitHub's own settings
store, not in the git tree, and writing them needs an
Administration-level credential no gate here holds.' The same is true
of the branch-protection ruleset scripts/land-stack.mjs itself reads
at merge time (gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}).
'.github/rulesets/**' is a PROPOSED, forward-declared glob: if this
repository ever gains a settings-as-code export of its branch
ruleset or repository settings (a real capability GitHub offers, not
adopted here yet), that path is tier-2 the moment it exists, with no
further decision needed to make it so. It matches no file today, so
it changes nothing about this pull request.
governance/model-qualifications/** IS real and matches today: the
model allowlist explicitly requires per-row owner approval
(approvedBy: "owner") before a row is meant to count as qualified for
C3 -- but `scripts/land-stack.mjs` does NOT read this file or enforce
it at all in this slice (an earlier draft of this comment, and of
docs/HITL.md, claimed otherwise; corrected). Reading and enforcing
model qualification is real, separate work for a later slice; this
path is tier-2 today because it is the OWNER-APPROVAL PROCESS for a
capability not yet wired in, not because anything currently consumes
it.
The remaining entries are the enforcement surface itself -- this file,
the conductor that reads it, the decision-record contract/validator,
the publishing scope, and gate helper modules -- added per #1187
review at 8e6d97ea, should-fix 13; see this file's own header comment.
A path glob used to authorize a tier-2 change via a decision record's
own `links.paths` (not this file) must be EITHER a literal path with no
glob metacharacters, OR EXACTLY ONE of this section's own `globs`
entries, verbatim -- enforced by scripts/land-stack.mjs's
`isOverbroadPathGlob`, computed against this actual tier config, not a
fixed canary-path list (#1187 review at df15ab87, blocking finding 4:
the canary approach let `governance/**`, `.github/**`, `scripts/lib/**`
and a bare `*.yml` glob all pass as 'not overbroad', none of them
enumerable against a small fixed set; #1187 review at 8e6d97ea,
blocking finding 4 was the first pass at this rule).
THE PUBLISH/DEPRECATE PATH IS TIER-2, NAMED EXACTLY (#1187 review round
5, both reviewers, measured): tier-2 is now the literal set of files
that themselves run `npm publish`, `npm deprecate`, or `npm unpublish`
-- scripts/publish-qualified-directory.mjs (the real `npm publish .`
call), scripts/publish-qualified-set.mjs (the owner-present publish
loop that dispatches it), scripts/deprecate-registry-version.mjs and
scripts/deprecate-legacy-packages.mjs (the real `npm deprecate` calls),
and the three workflow files that run them --
.github/workflows/publish.yml, .github/workflows/deprecate-registry-
version.yml, .github/workflows/deprecate-legacy-packages.yml. Verified
by grepping every scripts/*.mjs and .github/workflows/*.yml for a
literal `npm publish`/`npm deprecate`/`npm unpublish` invocation (not a
comment or a string constant) on 2026-09-23; these four scripts and
three workflows are the whole result.
ROUND-4'S `scripts/publish-*.mjs` / `scripts/deprecate-*.mjs`-STYLE
WILDCARD GLOBS ARE GONE (#1187 review round 5, both reviewers,
blocking): a trailing `*` on each of those also matched
publish-qualified-directory.test.mjs, publish-qualified-set.test.mjs,
publish-workflow.test.mjs, deprecate-registry-version.test.mjs and
deprecate-legacy-packages.test.mjs -- an ordinary test-file edit
reached tier-2 and needed an owner decision record, measured by both
reviewers as the majority of the resulting owner-only regression over
the last 200 merges (see docs/HITL.md and this pull request's own body
for the re-run measurement). Every literal filename above names only
the executable; its `*.test.mjs` sibling is not listed and therefore
classifies tier-1 like any other scripts/** path.
validate-candidate-publish.mjs, select-publishable-packages.mjs,
run-candidate-qualification.mjs and set-scope.mjs -- round 4's other
four tier-2 entries -- are REMOVED from tier-2 for the same reason:
grepped directly, none of them contains a literal `npm publish`, `npm
deprecate` or `npm unpublish` invocation. Each GATES what is eligible
to publish or under which scope, which is real leverage over the
outcome, but is not itself the irreversible external action the
decision-tier rule at #1187 comment 5800142871 lists under tier 2 --
and each already classifies tier-1 via the broad `scripts/**` glob
above, so this is a narrowing of tier-2, not a loss of review
coverage. If a later slice finds one of these four scripts' own logic
changes are themselves being waved through without adequate review,
the fix is to re-add that one specific literal filename here with its
own dated rationale, not to restore a wildcard.
docs/HITL.md AND governance/decisions/hitl-escalation-rule*.json ARE
TIER-2 (#1187 escalation-rule round 2, both reviewers, blocking).
docs/HITL.md is the living, applied copy of the owner-ratified
escalation rule -- governance/decisions/hitl-escalation-rule.json's
own closing clause states plainly that changing the rule is an
authority change and 'legitimately your call' (the owner's), and that
'Agents can't write to the rule file or the deny hook'. Before this
entry, the MECHANICAL, path-based classification this file computes
put docs/HITL.md at tier-0 (it is prose, matched by none of the globs
above) and the decision record itself at tier-1 (via the broad
governance/** glob, since governance/decisions/** carries no
carve-out into tier1RecordExempt) -- exactly the porousness the
ratified rule's own path-mechanical assignment (Accepted item 2:
'Tiers are assigned mechanically, by the path rules') would otherwise
leave open: an edit to the rule's own living text or its durable
record could land with two ordinary reviewers, never reaching the
owner, contradicting the very rule being edited. `governance/decisions/
hitl-escalation-rule*.json` (a glob, not the one literal filename) also
covers any future SUPERSEDING record of the rule -- decision records
are append-only, so amending the rule later means a new file, not an
edit to this one, and that new file needs to classify tier-2 too,
without waiting on a separate, later addition to this list. A
superseding record must still follow this repository's naming
convention (prefixed with the id it supersedes, as
governance/decisions/weekly-release-calendar-owner-chat.json already
does for a different record) for this glob to reach it.
Enforced by scripts/land-stack.mjs's evaluateTier2Decision: at least
one governance/decisions/*.json record that is itself schema-valid,
`tier: "tier-2"`, `status: "decided"`, `decidedBy: "owner"`, not
superseded, not a relaxation past its own sunset, with an `expiry`
that parses and is in the future (an unparseable expiry is treated
as already expired), and linked to this change either by
pull-request number (links.pullRequests) or by a non-overbroad path
glob covering every tier-2 path the pull request touches
(links.paths). See docs/contracts/decision-record.json.
